title: “Lanterns” reveals John Stewart’s shocking origin in praised episode
seoTitle: “Lanterns” reveals John Stewart’s shocking origin in.
subtitle: The third episode of the series explores the Green Lantern’s past and the influence of his parents, who shaped him in a peculiar way.
excerpt: Character John Stewart became one of the most searched after the airing of the third episode of “Lanterns”.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Character John Stewart is trending in searches after the airing of the third episode of the series “Lanterns”, which delivered a new, detailed origin story for the hero. The chapter, considered the strongest of the season so far, explores the making of the Green Lantern in an unprecedented way and introduces a crucial new character.

A new origin for John Stewart

Episode 3 of “Lanterns” dives into John Stewart’s past with a non‑linear narrative that fills gaps about his childhood, his relationship with his parents, his military career and his recruitment into the Green Lantern Corps. The series largely invents this origin story, distancing itself from the comics while retaining elements such as his mother’s influence and the Guardians of Oa’s oversight.

The show’s approach to Stewart’s origin is described as a successful risk, offering something different from typical superhero tales centered on the loss of a parental figure. Instead of an orphan, John is portrayed with very present and active parents, which, according to the series, may have been detrimental.

The parents’ influence on the hero’s formation

John Stewart’s parents, John Sr. (played by J. Alphonse Nicholson) and Bernadette (played by Nicole Ari Parker), are complex figures. They are shown as strong, powerful role models. Bernadette, in particular, serves as a voice for the series’ racial themes, repeatedly reminding her son and husband that they must fight to be heard in a universe that doesn’t value them.

However, their devotion borders on abuse, with scenes that include shooting apples off their son’s head or leaving him alone in a dangerous part of Chicago‑Midway City. Their obsession with turning him into a super‑soldier shapes John’s life in profound ways. Aaron Pierre, who plays adult John, is praised for conveying the silent emotional turbulence the character endures in his military and school life.

The debut of a Guardian of Oa

The third episode also marks the introduction of Laura Linney’s character, a Guardian of Oa in human form. Her appearance is described as a “consequential encounter” with John Stewart. Linney is lauded for her performance, portraying a character who seems ordinary yet is distinctly alien.

Hal Jordan’s past and the series’ plot

While the main focus is John Stewart, episode 3 also offers a glimpse of Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) wearing the classic Green Lantern domino mask in an old, grainy news clip. This archival material establishes that the series’ world already had a public superhero decades before Superman, without indicating a resurrection of Hal, who was confirmed dead in the pilot episode in 2026.

The show has used decades‑old broadcasts to build its timeline. Additionally, the 48‑hour deadline given by Antaan (Paul Ben‑Victor) for John to find the Manhunter in Rushville before a nuclear device is activated over Nebraska is set to expire in this episode. Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen), who is incarcerated and met Hal in 2016, mentioned the Manhunter as a major threat.

Episode 3 of “Lanterns” aired on Sunday, August 30, at 9 p.m. ET on HBO and HBO Max. The eight‑episode season will conclude on October 4.

With information from IGN, FanBolt.
